newsitem.title: UK: Dollar firmer in Europe but recent ranges persist.
newsitem.headline: Dollar firmer in Europe but recent ranges persist.

text.p: The dollar edged higher in morning Europe against the mark and yen but still within recent ranges and in fairly quiet trade, said dealers.

The dollar continued its firmer trend started overnight with dollar/yen finding support from comments from Japan's senior Ministry of Finance official Eisuke Sakakibara that Japan's forex policy would remain unchanged.

Japan's Economic Planning Agency Minister Taro Aso added to the bid dollar/yen tone by saying the pace of rises in Japan's trade surplus is likely to slow from the autumn. The rising surplus has been a key factor in recent yen strength.
Japanese May current account data is due overnight Tuesday and is expected to confirm rising trade surplus environment.
"Historically, there is a good relationship with a rising current account surplus and a strong yen," said Mark Geddes, treasury economist at ABN-Amro in London.
However, Geddes also said the market has already positioned itself for yen strength and further confirmation of a rising surplus may only produce limited yen gains from here.
Dollar/yen was trading at 113.05/15 against 112.70/75 late Monday in Europe. Mark/yen was also firmer at 64.43/46 from 64.31/34 on Monday.
Dollar/mark gained slightly after data showed pan-German June unemployment rose a seasonally adjusted 11,000 to 4.37 million, slightly above an average of analysts' forecasts.

"The three-month average for this time of the year is worse than last year, the worst in labour market is not over yet," said Guenther Redeker, analyst at Chase Investment Bank speaking on Reuters Financial Television.

Today's jobless rise is seen reinforcing expectations of a soft euro, as the data puts further pressure on Germany's budget plans. A supplementary budget for this year and a full 1998 budget is to be presented on Friday.
Dollar/mark was trading at 1.7560/65 at 0817 GMT against 1.7504/09 late Monday in Europe. The mark was steady on its European crosses, little moved on the jobs figures.

Sterling, meantime, recovered from Monday's lows against the mark, finding support mainly from continuing expectations of a UK rate rise coming out of the Wednesday/Thursday Bank of England monetary policy committee meeting.
The pound stood at 2.9575/85 marks from 2.9540/50 late Monday.
